$comment: Declarative source of truth for the OpenClaw runtime layer. Edit + redeploy to apply. Read by bootstrap.sh.

wrappers.name: mcporter
wrappers.description: Inject --config so mcporter always reads the persistent mcporter.json on /data

wrappers.name: gws
wrappers.description: Inject default Google Workspace credentials path

symlinks.description: Default mcporter config path expected by /app — points at persistent copy

Same sanitised-PATH problem as granola below, and this one was silently breaking automations: the mcporter wrapper lives in /data/.openclaw/bin (not /data/npm/bin), which is also off the agent Bash PATH. Both the bdm Attio and growth-marketing Google Ads cron jobs failed every run with 'Bash failed: mcporter list <server> --schema' until this link existed.

Google Workspace CLI wrapper (injects the service-account credentials path). Backs the gws-shared/gws-docs/gws-docs-write/gws-drive/gws-drive-upload skills on main, bdm and growth-marketing — all of which were unreachable from the agent Bash tool without this link.

The agent Bash tool runs with a SANITISED PATH that excludes /data/npm/bin — only /usr/local/{s}bin, /usr/{s}bin and /{s}bin. Without this link an agent calling `granola` gets 'command not found' (exit 127) and has to recover by guessing the absolute path. /usr/local/bin is in the image, so the link is recreated on every boot; the target lives on /data.
Same sanitised-PATH problem as granola above.

Notion CLI (npm `ntn`), used by the built-in `notion` skill. Same sanitised-PATH problem as granola above — and /usr/local/bin lives in the image, so without this the link is lost on every redeploy even though the CLI itself persists on /data.

secrets.$comment: Resolved at boot from 1Password with the `op` CLI, using a service-account token in the OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN env var (set it as a Railway variable — never commit it). INERT by design: with no token, or if a fetch fails, bootstrap leaves the existing on-disk secrets exactly as they are and only warns. It never fails the boot and never writes an empty value over a good one, so a 1Password outage cannot take the bot down.

provisioned.name: environment
provisioned.description: Shared environment facts for EVERY agent (what persists, where to install, shell gotchas, off-limits paths). Copied into <workspace>/env/AGENTS.md for the whole live roster and overwritten on every boot; injected into every turn by the bootstrap-extra-files hook (hooks.internal.entries in openclaw.json, paths ["env/AGENTS.md"] - runtime config, not written here). The basename must stay AGENTS.md and the file must stay inside the workspace, or the hook ignores it.

provisioned.name: shopify
provisioned.description: Client Shopify store access: shopify-admin CLI + the `shopify` skill, restored onto /data from the image on every boot so a redeploy, upgrade or lost volume cannot drop it. Tokens are NOT provisioned — they live only in /data/.openclaw/credentials/shopify/tokens.env (0600) or Railway variables.

seed_files.$comment: Seeded ONLY if absent — never overwrites the live registry, which is where client stores are added at runtime.

provisioned.name: granola
provisioned.description: Granola meeting notes: the `granola` CLI (public-api.granola.ai, read-only) + the `granola` skill, restored onto /data from the image on every boot. The API key is NOT provisioned — it lives only in /data/.openclaw/credentials/granola/token.env (0600), seeded from 1Password when a service-account token is present.

snapshot.$comment: Tar.gz to /data/snapshots/preboot-${commit}.tar.gz before each deploy. Keep last N. /data/.openclaw/state holds openclaw.sqlite (cron jobs, sessions, credential store) since 2026.7.1 migrated them out of the JSON files — it is the snapshot that actually matters for rollback. cron/jobs.json is retained for pre-2026.7.1 installs and is normally jobs.json.migrated now.

prune_backups.$comment: Stop accumulating openclaw.json.bak* clutter — keep newest 3

documentation.$comment: Informational only — used by bootstrap to print a deploy summary. Not enforced.

known_unmanaged_binaries.note: User-uploaded 25 MB binary (UID 501). Not managed by manifest; persists naturally on /data.
